claims.statement: By geometric morphometrics (Procrustes distances), the octanol-induced head shapes of G. dorotocephala regenerates are closer to the wild-type head shapes of the species they resemble than to the wild-type G. dorotocephala head shape.
claims.quote: Comparisons of the Procrustes distances between shape groups (Figure 2A, Table 1) showed that the experimentally derived morphologies were closer in shape to the wild-type morphologies they resembled than the wild-type Girardia dorotocephala head morphology.
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.2. Quantitative Comparison of Induced vs. Genome-Specific Head Shapes

claims.label: Induced head shapes are stochastic, with frequencies tracking evolutionary distance
claims.statement: Under identical octanol treatment, G. dorotocephala regenerates take one of several discrete head shapes, and the frequencies of the shapes are unequal and correlate roughly with the evolutionary distance (from rRNA phylogeny) between G. dorotocephala and the species each shape resembles, with shapes of closer relatives (S. mediterranea, D. japonica) more frequent than that of the more distant P. felina.
claims.quote: We conclude that not only are phenotypic outcomes from physiological network perturbation stochastic (as the same treatment leads to one of several discrete shapes among individuals), but the frequencies are not equal and correlate roughly with evolutionary distance between the worm species these heads resemble.
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.3. The Head Shape Changes Are Stochastic

claims.label: Gap-junction-perturbed worms also acquire the brain shape of the species they resemble
claims.statement: G. dorotocephala regenerates whose heads resemble another species after octanol treatment also have brain morphologies (length/width ratio, by anti-synapsin staining) resembling the brains of wild-type worms of that species.
claims.quote: Strikingly, we found that pseudo worms possessed brain morphologies that look like the brain morphologies of wild-type worms whose head shapes they resembled (Figure 4D–F) (ANOVA, p < 0.001).
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.4. Brain Structure of GJ-Perturbed Worms Is Also Altered to That of Other Species

claims.label: Perturbed worms adopt the anterior stem-cell distribution of the species they resemble
claims.statement: In octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates, the transformation toward another species' head shape extends to the species-characteristic distribution of neoblasts (mitotic stem cells) in the anterior body, and the authors conclude that the patterning processes disrupted by gap junction perturbation also organize the distribution of mitotically active cells.
claims.quote: We conclude that the transformation of G. dorotocephala worms to resemble other species also extends to the species-specific, characteristic internal distribution of their stem cells, and that the patterning processes that are disrupted after GJC perturbation are also responsible for organizing the distribution of mitotically active cells.
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.5. Distribution of Neoblasts Is Altered to That of Other Species in GJ-Perturbed Worms

claims.label: Octanol-treated worms show more isopotential regions, which return to normal by 30 days
claims.statement: Ten days after transient octanol exposure, regenerated G. dorotocephala show more distinct isopotential (membrane-voltage) regions by DiBAC dye imaging than controls, and the number of isopotential regions returns to the wild-type level after 30 days of morphological remodeling.
claims.quote: We detected an increased number of isopotential regions in the pseudo worms compared to the states of control worms; interestingly, the numbers of isopotential regions return to those of a wild-type state after 30 days of morphological remodeling (Figure 6I).

claims.label: Induced head shapes remodel back toward G. dorotocephala after regeneration ends
claims.statement: The other-species head shapes induced in G. dorotocephala by octanol are not permanent: between days 10 and 30, after regeneration is complete and without further injury, the heads are remodeled to more closely resemble wild-type G. dorotocephala.
claims.quote: We found that the induced morphologies were remodeled, long after regenerative processes had ended, to produce morphologies that bore closer resemblance to wild-type G. dorotocephala.

claims.label: Head remodeling passes from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to normal shape
claims.statement: In canonical variate shape space, the D. japonica head morphology lies between those of G. dorotocephala and S. mediterranea, and octanol-induced S. mediterranea-like G. dorotocephala heads remodel by moving from S. mediterranea-like to D. japonica-like to G. dorotocephala morphology.
claims.quote: DJ morphology lies between GD and SM morphologies in this space, and we observe remodeling that moves from SM morphology to DJ morphology to GD morphology.

claims.label: Agent-based model of migrating, signaling cells reproduces the observed head shapes
claims.statement: In an agent-based model of planarian head regeneration in which static somatic cells emit a chemical signal and migratory cells (neoblasts or their progeny) are repelled by it, deactivating different subsets of signaling cells (representing octanol gap-junction blockade) reproduces the four observed head shapes, so a small set of gap-junction-regulated cell behaviors such as migration and cell-cell signaling can quantitatively explain the observed morphologies.
claims.quote: We conclude that a small set of cell-level behaviors, such as migration and cell-cell signaling that are known to be regulated by GJC and thus are perturbed by octanol exposure [35,39,49,98,101,102], can quantitatively explain the morphologies we observed in planaria.

claims.label: Coherent discrete head shapes show the octanol effect is instructive rather than toxic
claims.statement: The octanol-induced head-shape change in G. dorotocephala is instructive rather than a toxic or housekeeping defect, because it yields one of several coherent, ecologically valid morphologies rather than regeneration failure or disorganized growth, with no intermediate morphologies observed.
claims.quote: The head morphology alteration effect was instructive, and not merely one of toxicity or a house-keeping defect, because the outcome was not merely disruption of regenerative ability or a generalized mis-patterning (e.g., tumor or other disorganized growth), but rather resulted in one of several coherent (and ecologically-valid) morphologies.

claims.label: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape
claims.statement: In G. dorotocephala, the same 3-day exposure to hexanol, a closely related alcohol that does not efficiently block gap junction channels, does not produce altered head morphologies, consistent with the head-shape change depending on octanol's gap-junction-blocking activity rather than a generalized effect of long-chain alcohols.
claims.quote: The same 3-day treatment with the closely related alcohol, hexanol (6-OH), which does not efficiently block gap junction channels, and subsequent regeneration in water for 7 days, did not produce altered morphologies, consistent with the importance of the GJ-blocking activity of octanol, and not some other generalized effect of long-chain alcohols.

claims.label: Bioelectric networks derive distinct morphologies from one genome
claims.statement: Physiological bioelectric networks are a previously unrecognized input by which distinct morphologies, including those of other species, can be derived from the same genome, as shown by gap-junction perturbation in G. dorotocephala.
claims.quote: Here, we identify a novel physiological input into the process by which distinct morphologies can be derived from the same genome: physiological bioelectric networks.

claims.label: Brief gap-junction blockade persistently alters bioelectric state after drug washout
claims.statement: In G. dorotocephala, the long-lasting alteration of bioelectric patterning after brief octanol exposure is not caused by residual octanol (which leaves tissues within 24 h) but is initiated by octanol's disruption of gap junction communication, which alters bioelectric network topology and results in a persistent perturbation of bioelectric state.
claims.quote: Although these long-lasting alterations in bioelectrical patterning are not directly caused by octanol remaining within the body of the worm (since 8-OH is known to depart planarian tissues within 24 h [20]), they are initiated by the octanol-mediated disruption of GJC, which alters bioelectric network topology, and results in persistent perturbation of bioelectric state.

claims.label: Partial, variable gap-junction blockade is consistent with stochastic head-shape outcomes
claims.statement: The variability and overall magnitude of the bioelectric effect imply that octanol only partially shuts down gap junction communication in each G. dorotocephala (affecting some percentage of gap junctions per animal), which the authors consider consistent with the stochasticity of the head-shape phenotype.
claims.quote: The variability and overall magnitude of the effect imply that the result of 8-OH exposure is only partially effective in shutting down GJC (affecting some percentage of GJs in any animal); this is consistent with the stochasticity of the morphological phenotype (Figure 3).

claims.label: Head shape may be encoded in time-dependent rather than steady voltage patterns
claims.statement: Because single-image voltage distributions showed no simple correspondence with the head shapes of octanol-treated G. dorotocephala, the authors consider it most likely that shape outcomes are encoded in time-dependent bioelectric activity rather than in steady voltage distributions, as in information encoding in the central nervous system.
claims.quote: The most likely explanation however is that shape outcomes may not be encoded via steady (single-image) distributions but in time-dependent activity, as occurs during information encoding in the central nervous system.

claims.label: Planarian morphology behaves as a homeostatic parameter maintained toward a target shape
claims.statement: In planarians, morphology appears to be a homeostatic parameter that is repeatedly assessed and adjusted to maintain a 'target' morphology: after an incorrect head shape is produced during regeneration, the mismatch with the target triggers remodeling (between days 10 and 17 in octanol-treated G. dorotocephala), even after large-scale reorganization has ended.
claims.quote: Morphology appears to be a homeostatic parameter, one that is consistently assessed and adjusted in order to maintain some “target” morphology.

claims.label: Gap-junction-dependent instructive signals pass from somatic tissue to neoblasts
claims.statement: The authors propose that significant instructive, gap-junction-dependent signaling passes from planarian somatic tissues to neoblasts or their progeny to guide new tissue generation and shaping during regeneration.
claims.quote: In this model, we propose that significant instructive (GJ-dependent) signaling occurs from the somatic tissues to the neoblasts or their progeny, to guide the new tissue generation and shaping during regeneration.

claims.label: Somatic cells can be modeled as a slow neural-like network obeying brain-like dynamics
claims.statement: The authors propose conceptualizing the link between gap junctional connectivity among planarian cells and discrete regenerative outcomes by viewing the cells as a neural-like network that processes developmental information more slowly but obeys the same statistical dynamics as the brain.
claims.quote: Thus, we propose that one way to conceptualize the linkage between bioelectrical connectivity among worm cells (GJC) and discrete global behavioral outcomes achieved by regeneration is to view the worms’ cells as a neural-like network, processing developmental information more slowly but obeying the same statistical dynamics rules as are known to occur in the brain (Figure 9A).

claims.label: Planarian head shapes may be attractors of a gap-junction-coupled bioelectric network
claims.statement: The authors hypothesize that distinct planarian head shapes may be attractors in the state space of the bioelectric network formed by body cells coupled by gap junctions, that these attractors correspond to regions of morphospace in the evolutionary sense, and that octanol knocks the network's stochastic dynamics into one of several nearby attractors normally belonging to other flatworm species.
claims.quote: We hypothesize that distinct shape outcomes may be attractors in a state space describing distinct modes of the bioelectric network of planarian body cells connected by gap junctions (electrical synapses); in essence, these attractors correspond to regions of a morphospace as classically understood by evolutionary theory [151].
claims.work: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms
claims.chapter: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace

claims.label: Regeneration as descent to a free-energy attractor; induced shapes as local minima
claims.statement: On the authors' proposed view, discrete planarian head patterns are the lowest free-energy outcomes of bioelectric network dynamics; amputation raises free energy and regeneration is a return to a low-energy attractor, octanol shifts the system to another attractor, and the induced other-species shapes are only local minima since worms return to the global minimum of G. dorotocephala morphology after about 3–4 weeks.
claims.quote: On this view (Figure 9), the discrete head patterns are outcomes of bioelectric network dynamics with the lowest free-energy; cutting the network raises the free energy by deviating the system from its optimal morphology (damage), and initiates the regenerative process—a journey back down to a low-energy attractor.

claims.label: Planarian evolutionary distance may reflect ease of shifting a shared patterning network
claims.statement: The authors suggest that a core network of gene-regulatory elements and gap-junction-mediated signals may be shared among many planarians, with species differences tweaking its dynamics, so that evolutionary distance between planarian species may reflect how easily this network can be shifted into its different outcome states, as during gap junction inhibition.
claims.quote: The evolutionary distance among the planarian types may thus be expected to reflect the ease of shifting this network into its different potential outcome states (as occurs during GJC inhibition).

claims.label: Resting potential of distant cells controls oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis
claims.statement: The resting membrane potentials of cells located at a distance from oncogene-expressing cells are critical for whether those oncogene-expressing cells go on to form tumors in vivo, as shown in Xenopus laevis tadpoles injected with human oncogenes.
claims.quote: Extending prior work focused on the bioelectric state of cancer cells themselves, we show for the first time that the resting potentials of distant cells are critical for oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis.

claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract

claims.label: Oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus share hallmarks of human tumors
claims.statement: Tumor-like structures induced in Xenopus laevis tadpoles by human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS display overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, intracellular acidity and leukocyte attraction, hallmarks shared with classic human tumors.
claims.quote: In the Xenopus laevis tadpole model, we used human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS to drive formation of tumor-like structures that exhibited overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, acidity, and leukocyte attraction.

claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract

claims.label: Remote Kv1.5 hyperpolarization suppresses tumor-like structures from two oncogenes
claims.statement: In Xenopus laevis embryos, misexpressing the hyperpolarizing potassium channel Kv1.5 in a blastomere distant from the oncogene-injected blastomere reduces the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 35% for Xrel3 and about 29% for Gli1, indicating the suppression is not specific to one oncogene.
claims.quote: Kv1.5-induced long-distance hyperpolarization was also able to significantly suppress Xrel3 and Gli1 ITLS formation by 34.9% (N=225; t-test, P<0.05) and 29.4% (N=292; t-test, P<0.05), respectively (Fig. 2C), suggesting the effect is not specific for just one type of oncogene.

claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS

claims.label: High-chloride hyperpolarization suppresses KRAS tumors, so the effect is ion-independent
claims.statement: Raising extracellular chloride, which hyperpolarizes cells through native chloride channels, decreases the incidence of KRASG12D-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis embryos by about 38%, showing that tumor suppression depends on the change in membrane voltage rather than on the Kv1.5 channel or on potassium specifically.
claims.quote: Treatment with high chloride (whose uptake by native Cl− channels hyperpolarizes cells) resulted in a 37.5% decrease (N=349; t-test P<0.05) in KRASG12D ITLS, demonstrating that the suppressive effect is not specific for Kv1.5 nor for potassium, as mediators of the crucial Vmem change (Fig. 2C).
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS

claims.label: Native CLIC1 mediates chloride-based long-range tumor suppression
claims.statement: The endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1) is required for chloride-driven, long-range suppression of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis, because non-local overexpression of wildtype CLIC1 increases suppression while a dominant-negative CLIC1C24S mutant blocks suppression even under high extracellular chloride.
claims.quote: In contrast, overexpression of the mutant CLIC1 (N=336) effectively blocked ITLS suppression despite the presence of high Cl− (Fig 4C). Together, these data suggest a role for native CLIC1 in mediating hyperpolarization-induced long-range ITLS suppression.
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Chloride-dependent hyperpolarization through endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1)

claims.label: HDAC1 activity transduces remote voltage change into tumor suppression
claims.statement: Histone deacetylase 1 activity is the main transduction step by which hyperpolarization of distant cells suppresses tumorigenesis in Xenopus laevis, since expressing a dominant-negative HDAC1 at a site remote from KRASG12D-expressing cells raises the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 36%.
claims.quote: introducing DN-HDAC1 non-locally to the site of KRASG12D increased ITLS formation incidence by 35.6% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 5C), suggesting a role for histone deacetylase 1 activity controlling cell behavior at a distance.

claims.label: Antibiotics against gram-positive bacteria increase tumor incidence
claims.statement: Treating Xenopus laevis embryos with antibiotics that target gram-positive bacteria — novobiocin alone, or a cocktail of gentamicin, metronidazole, vancomycin and clindamycin — significantly increases the incidence of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures, implying that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain tumorigenesis.
claims.quote: Finally, a cocktail of antibiotics (gentamicin, metrodinazole, vancomycin hydrochloride, and clindamycin hydrochloride, all at 20 μM concentration) targeting gram-positive bacteria resulted in a significant increase in ITLS incidence by 26.2% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 6).

claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Changes in Vmem

claims.label: Vmem controls tumorigenesis via bacterially derived butyrate acting on HDAC1
claims.statement: Control of oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis by resting membrane potential in Xenopus laevis is mediated by histone deacetylase 1, whose inhibition depends on butyrate produced by native gram-positive bacteria.
claims.quote: Together, these data suggest that the control of tumorigenesis by Vmem is mediated by HDAC1, via butyrate derived from gram-positive bacteria.

claims.label: Tumors may themselves emit bioelectric information detectable at a distance
claims.statement: The authors speculate that long-range bioelectric connections in tumorigenesis are bidirectional, so that in addition to remote tissue voltage influencing tumor growth, tumors may emit bioelectric information that could be detected at a distance.
claims.quote: It is tempting to speculate that the long-range connections are bi-directional: not only does remote electrical state of tissue matter for tumor growth, but perhaps tumors also emit bioelectrical information that could be detectable at a distance.

claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem

claims.label: Resting potential as a systems-level causal factor rather than specific channels
claims.statement: Because tumor suppression was obtained with either chloride- or potassium-based hyperpolarization, the authors argue that a systems-level physiological property — resting membrane potential — rather than any specific ion channel acting as an oncogene or tumor suppressor, can be a powerful causal factor regulating tumorigenesis.
claims.quote: Thus, in complement to the gene-focused idea of specific ion channels being intrinsic oncogenes or tumor suppressors [44, 48, 145], we suggest that a systems-level physiological property – resting potential – can be a powerful causal factor in regulating these processes.
claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem

claims.label: Hyperpolarization skews butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells
claims.statement: In the model the authors propose, hyperpolarized cells present a positively charged outer surface that reduces bacterial viability, so butyrate-producing bacteria are distributed away from hyperpolarized cells and toward the depolarized oncogene-expressing cells, where the resulting butyrate inhibits HDAC and promotes histone hyperacetylation and cell cycle arrest.
claims.quote: As a result, distribution of butyrate producing-bacteria is skewed away from hyperpolarized cells in favor of oncogene-expressing cells, which are known to be depolarized pre-neoplastic transformation [43].

claims.label: If conserved in mammals, Vmem modulation offers cancer detection and treatment routes
claims.statement: The authors predict that if the role of remote endogenous bioelectric states in tumorigenesis is conserved in mammalian cancer models, modulation of resting membrane potential — potentially with ion channel drugs already approved for human use — would provide new cancer detection and treatment modalities.
claims.quote: Future work must also examine the roles of remote endogenous bioelectric states in mammalian cancer models; if conserved, these data suggest a number of detection and treatment modalities focused on Vmem modulation.

claims.label: Embryonic nicotine exposure causes major brain malformations in Xenopus
claims.statement: Exposing Xenopus laevis embryos to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35) causes major brain morphology defects (absent nostrils, forebrain or midbrain, misformed hindbrain) in about 55% of tadpoles at stage 45, compared with about 6% of controls.
claims.quote: Nicotine exposure caused a significantly high incidence of major brain morphology defects (~55%) in comparison to controls (~6%).

claims.label: BETSE model: leak and Kir channels produce a hyperpolarized neural tube prepattern
claims.statement: In a BETSE bioelectric model of the stage 15 Xenopus neurula, regional differences in K+ and Cl− leak permeability open Kir channels in the neural tube, producing a Vmem of about −50 mV there while the neural folds and ectoderm stay near −5 mV, matching observed embryonic Vmem patterns.
claims.quote: This results in open Kir channels in the hyperpolarized neural tube region leading to a Vmem pattern of approximately −50 mV in the neural tube region, while the lateral neural folds and ectoderm remain at ~−5 mV (Fig. 3a, e).

claims.label: Nicotine depolarizes the neural plate prepattern by about 15 mV, as the model predicted
claims.statement: In stage 15 Xenopus embryos, nicotine treatment significantly reduces the endogenous neural hyperpolarization signal (a depolarization of about 15 mV, measured by calibrated voltage-dye imaging), matching the BETSE model's prediction in direction and magnitude.
claims.quote: Nicotine-treated embryos showed significant reduction in endogenous neural Vmem signal (depolarization by ~15 mV) in comparison to controls (Figs. 4a, b, e, f, and Supplementary Figure 1). This observation matches the BETSE model predictions of nicotine effect on Vmem both in direction (depolarization) and magnitude (~15 mV).

claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Nicotine targets Vmem

claims.label: Nicotine causes brain defects by disrupting the endogenous bioelectric prepattern
claims.statement: The authors' BETSE model explains nicotine-induced brain defects in Xenopus as resulting from nicotine's disruption of the endogenous bioelectric prepattern (neural tube hyperpolarization) required for brain development.
claims.quote: Our model explains why nicotine induces brain defects: it correctly predicts the disruptive effects of this teratogen on the endogenous bioelectric prepattern required for brain development.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Nicotine targets Vmem

claims.label: Normal brain patterning needs the Vmem difference between neural tube and lateral tissue
claims.statement: In Xenopus brain development, it is the spatial contrast of Vmem that matters: depolarizing the neural tube region or hyperpolarizing the lateral regions both cause brain defects, because the precise differential bioelectric state induces the balance of proliferation, apoptosis and gene expression needed to build a normal brain.
claims.quote: The spatial patterning is crucial, as both depolarization of the middle region, or hyperpolarization of the lateral regions, both cause brain defects—it is the precise differential bioelectric state that induces the required balance of proliferation, apoptosis, and gene expression to build a normal brain28,48.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent

claims.label: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients
claims.statement: In the BETSE model of the Xenopus neurula, HCN2 channels open at hyperpolarized membrane voltage and hyperpolarize further when open, so they act as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small existing Vmem gradients: sufficiently negative neural tube cells go very hyperpolarized while depolarized lateral regions are left unchanged.
claims.quote: HCN2 channels are predicted to open at hyperpolarized Vmem, generating more hyperpolarization with opening, thereby serving as a Vmem-controlled switch of Vmem state, capable of amplifying small Vmem gradients, similar to IT effect (Fig. 3c, e, f).
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent

claims.label: BETSE model predicts HCN2 maintains the neural tube Vmem pattern despite nicotine
claims.statement: The BETSE model predicts that uniformly expressed HCN2 channels, which open at hyperpolarized Vmem and so amplify small Vmem gradients, open preferentially in the Xenopus neural tube and maintain its hyperpolarized Vmem pattern even in nicotine-exposed model embryos.
claims.quote: Importantly, our model predicts that HCN2 expression leads to maintenance of neural tube Vmem pattern even in nicotine-exposed model embryos, similar to the action of IT (Fig. 3c vs. d, e, f).
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent

claims.label: Measured HCN2 hyperpolarization in vivo was about half the model's prediction
claims.statement: Hcn2 mRNA injection hyperpolarized the neural Vmem signal of Xenopus embryos by about 15 mV relative to controls, whereas the BETSE model predicted about 30 mV.
claims.quote: However, the extent of enhanced hyperpolarization predicted by BETSE model for IT and HCN2 was higher (~30 mV) than actually observed (~15 mV) (Figs. 3e and 4).
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem

claims.label: HCN2 expression restores the neural Vmem prepattern despite nicotine
claims.statement: In nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos, expression of HCN2 channels enhances the neural-tube-specific hyperpolarization and restores the endogenous Vmem prepattern that nicotine otherwise suppresses, as the BETSE model predicted.
claims.quote: As predicted, nicotine exposure suppresses the neural brain-specific Vmem pattern, while HCN2 channel expression enhances the neural Vmem pattern and restores it even in presence of the otherwise teratogenic nicotine.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem

claims.label: HCN2 reduces even minor background brain defects in untreated embryos
claims.statement: In untreated Xenopus embryos, Hcn2 mRNA injection reduced the incidence of minor deviations from ideal brain morphology from about 9% to about 1.5%, so HCN2 improved patterning beyond that of unperturbed controls.
claims.quote: Thus, misexpression of HCN2 channels resulted in an improvement of developmental patterning even beyond that observed in control populations of unperturbed embryos raised under optimal conditions.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 overexpression reduces background brain defects

claims.label: HCN2 fully rescues nicotine-induced brain malformations to control levels
claims.statement: Injection of Hcn2-WT mRNA into nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos reduced the incidence of major brain morphology defects from about 60% to about 6%, indistinguishable from untreated controls (about 7%).
claims.quote: Remarkably, Hcn2-WT mRNA-injected embryos showed a complete rescue of brain morphology defects from nicotine exposure, to levels (~6%) indistinguishable from that of untreated control embryos (~7%) (Fig. 5f).
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects

claims.label: Dominant-negative HCN2 does not rescue nicotine brain defects
claims.statement: Nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos injected with a dominant-negative, non-conducting HCN2 mutant showed no rescue of brain morphology defects (about 70% defective), so the rescue depends on HCN2 channel conductance.
claims.quote: In contrast, nicotine-exposed embryos injected with a mutant, dominant-negative form of HCN2 failed to show rescue of brain morphology defects (~70%) (Fig. 5f).
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects

claims.label: HCN2 restores wild-type brain shape in nicotine-exposed tadpoles
claims.statement: Geometric morphometrics of stage-45 tadpoles show that nicotine significantly changes brain shape relative to the head, while nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA do not differ in shape from controls.
claims.quote: Thus, nicotine significantly changes brain shape, but Hcn2-WT mRNA microinjections restore brain morphology to the wild-type state.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects

claims.label: HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed tadpoles
claims.statement: In an automated red-light avoidance assay, only about 12% of nicotine-exposed Xenopus tadpoles learned, versus 100% of controls, and about 85% of nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA learned.
claims.quote: However, nicotine-exposed embryos receiving Hcn2-WT mRNA showed significant improvement in learning ability (85%, n = 20) in comparison to nicotine-exposed tadpoles (Fig. 7b, c, ANOVA, p < 0.001).
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed larvae

claims.label: HCN2 rescue corrects otx2 and xbf1 expression after nicotine
claims.statement: Nicotine reduces or mispatterns expression of the forebrain/midbrain transcription factors otx2 and xbf1 in Xenopus embryos, and Hcn2-WT mRNA injection restores their normal expression, linking HCN2-mediated repair to the known genetic cascade of brain patterning.
claims.quote: Thus, HCN2 channel rescue of nicotine-induced defects includes correction of otx2 and xbf1, connecting HCN2-mediated repair of brain to the known molecular-genetic cascade of brain patterning factors.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 restores marker expression in nicotine-treated embryos

claims.label: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning
claims.statement: Because a dominant-negative HCN2 construct does not disrupt brain patterning, native HCN2 channel activity is not required for normal Xenopus brain patterning, ruling out the possibility that nicotine causes defects by directly blocking endogenous HCN2.
claims.quote: However, our experiments with dominant-negative HCN2 channel shows that native HCN2 channel activity is not required for proper brain patterning (Supplementary Figure 4), thus negating this possibility.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion

claims.label: HCN2's restorative action may extend to many teratogens and lesions
claims.statement: The authors suggest that HCN2's ability to improve brain morphology even in control embryos points to a general mechanism, reinforcing endogenous bioelectric signals needed for correct brain morphology, that could repair defects caused by a wide range of teratogens or physiological and genetic lesions, not only nicotine.
claims.quote: These observations suggest that the restorative action of HCN2 is not limited to nicotine-induced brain morphology defects, but could reveal a more general mechanism of action, reinforcing the endogenous bioelectrical signals required for correct developmental brain morphology that might be partially destabilized by a wide range of exogenous teratogens or endogenous physiological/genetic lesions.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion

claims.label: Reagents that sharpen bioelectric compartment borders reinforce normal patterning
claims.statement: The BETSE model predicts that reagents that sharpen the borders between bioelectric compartments, such as the context-sensitive HCN2 channel, will reinforce normal developmental patterning, a prediction confirmed for HCN2 in vivo.
claims.quote: Most importantly, it predicts that reagents that sharpen borders between bioelectric compartments will reinforce normal patterning, thus identifying a context-sensitive HCN2 ion channel as an intervention tool.
claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion

claims.label: A Self is bounded by a cognitive light cone of events it can measure and affect
claims.statement: Any Self (agent) is demarcated by a computational surface, the spatio-temporal boundary of the events it can measure, model and try to affect; this surface is a cognitive "light cone" that sets the scale and limits of its cognition and allows agents of very different material make-up to be compared.
claims.quote: Any Self is demarcated by a computational surface – the spatio-temporal boundary of events that it can measure, model, and try to affect. This surface sets a functional boundary - a cognitive “light cone” which defines the scale and limits of its cognition.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Abstract

claims.label: Somatic cells kept their computational capacities and scaled them to anatomical goals
claims.statement: Somatic cells did not lose the behavioural plasticity and computational capabilities of their unicellular ancestors when they became part of metazoan bodies; they scaled them to pursue larger goals, namely building and maintaining complex anatomies.
claims.quote: somatic cells did not lose their behavioral plasticity and computational capabilities in becoming part of metazoan swarms (bodies): they scaled them to enable pursuit of larger goals consisting of creation and upkeep of massively complex anatomies (Pezzulo and Levin, 2015).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Cell collectives pursue organ-level target morphologies despite perturbation
claims.statement: Regulative development and regeneration (e.g. scrambled tadpole faces that still become normal frog faces, tail grafts remodelling into limbs, kidney tubules of constant diameter despite enlarged cells) show that somatic cells pursue specific target morphologies despite perturbation, with set points that are large organ-level macrostates not defined at the single-cell level.
claims.quote: They reveal the ability of somatic cells to not only pursue specific target morphologies despite perturbations and novel scenarios, but to pursue collective patterning outcomes that are truly enormous with respect to the scale of size and organization of single cells
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Cell domains make coordinated group decisions, even random ones
claims.statement: Cells join into domains that make decisions as a single unit: when left-right asymmetry is randomized in early embryos, a whole domain picks L or R identity rather than individual cells choosing independently, and in frog melanoma-like conversion all melanocytes in a body convert or not together.
claims.quote: Remarkably, however, this randomization is made on a group level – in each case, the entire domain randomly picks L or R identity, not exhibiting a speckled appearance where each cell adopts a stochastic outcome. The decision is random, but all of the cells in the domain are coordinated to make the same random decision (Levin et al., 2002).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Neural motor control may be an exaptation of bioelectric navigation of morphospace
claims.statement: Neural control of body movement in three-dimensional space may be an evolutionary exaptation and speed-up of an older, slower role of bioelectric signalling: moving the body's configuration through anatomical morphospace during embryogenesis, repair and remodelling.
claims.quote: Neural networks control the movement of a body in three-dimensional space; this scheme may be an evolutionary exaptation and speed-optimization of a more ancient, slower role of bioelectrical signaling: the movement of body configuration through anatomical morphospace during embryogenesis, repair, and remodeling (Sullivan et al., 2016; Mathews and Levin, 2018; Mclaughlin and Levin, 2018).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Brain cognition lies on a continuum with conserved pre-neural computation
claims.statement: Given the deep evolutionary conservation of ion-channel and neurotransmitter mechanisms between developmental and behavioural processes, the cognitive capacities of advanced brains are likely on a continuum with, and evolved from, much simpler computational processes conserved at both the functional and molecular levels.
claims.quote: Thus, it is likely that the cognitive capacities of advanced brains lie on a continuum with, and evolve from, much simpler computational processes that are widely conserved at both the functional and mechanism (molecular) levels.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Disrupting or restoring cell communication should trigger or suppress cancer
claims.statement: The shrinking-Self view of cancer predicts that interfering with physiological communication among cells should be able to trigger cancer and restoring it should suppress cancer, and that the relevant parameter (communication) is spread over considerable distance rather than confined to single cells as genomic damage is.
claims.quote: This view predicts that interference with (or restoration of) physiological communication among cells should be able to trigger (or suppress) cancer and that the relevant parameter (communication) is spread out over considerable distance and not confined to single cells (e.g., genomic damage).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: Depolarization induces and hyperpolarization prevents tumour-like changes in tadpoles
claims.statement: In tadpoles, depolarizing a specific cell population is sufficient to cause metastatic-like transformation of normal melanocytes in genetically normal animals, while optogenetic or constitutive hyperpolarization prevents human oncogenes from inducing tumours.
claims.quote: metastatic transformation of normal melanocytes can be achieved in genetically normal tadpoles simply by depolarizing a specific cell population (Lobikin et al., 2012), while, conversely, human oncogenes which normally induce tumors can be prevented from doing so simply by optogenetic or constitutive hyperpolarization (Chernet and Levin, 2013b, 2014; Chernet et al., 2015, 2016).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: Cancer cells are no more selfish than normal cells; their self is smaller
claims.statement: Cells in a metazoan body are not less selfish than unicellular organisms or cancer cells; all are equally selfish, but the self that normal somatic cells defend is larger in space, time and complexity, its boundary being set by how far information passes between subunits.
claims.quote: They are equally selfish, working only for the benefit of themselves, but the relevant self that they defend is bigger in terms of space, time, and complexity. As will be argued below, what defines this Self is the boundary of information being able to pass between the subunits.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: Most biological systems consist of multiple nested selves
claims.statement: Under Scale-Free Cognition, most biological systems consist of multiple, nested selves rather than one, each inner agent maintaining its own Self only to the extent that it restricts information flow from its neighbours.
claims.quote: It is an essential aspect of Scale-Free Cognition that most biological systems consist of multiple, nested selves [not one, as implied by Integrated Information Theory (Tononi, 2008)].
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: An Individual is defined by the scale and types of goals it can pursue
claims.statement: The scale and types of goals (in the cybernetic sense of feedback toward a specific state) that a system can pursue define the boundaries and content of that system as an agent or Individual; the coherent Self is the set of parts that operate together toward specific goal states.
claims.quote: I propose a definition of an Individual based on its information-processing structure (Barandiaran et al., 2009): the scale and types of goals that a system can pursue defines (determines) the boundaries and content of the putative “agent.”
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective

claims.label: Cognitive light cones have expanded over evolutionary time
claims.statement: The volume of possible cognitive light cones (spatio-temporal boundaries of agents' goals) has presumably kept expanding over evolutionary time, through innovations in body structure that drastically enlarge the cognitive boundary, although some lineages contract it permanently or in particular life stages.
claims.quote: Presumably, the volume of possible cognitive light cones keeps expanding with evolutionary time (although some lineages can contract it, permanently or during specific ontogenetic life stages). Over evolutionary scales, there have been “inflationary leaps” – innovations in body structure which drastically increase the cognitive boundary of viable selves.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective

claims.label: Memory and learning are the origin of developmental modularity
claims.statement: Memory can be the beginning of modularity because learning compresses complex states into simple triggers; in somatic control networks this appears as developmental modules in which a single simple driver (e.g. a bioelectric state) initiates a complex morphogenetic cascade such as building an eye or hand.
claims.quote: Importantly, memory can serve as the beginning of modularity because learning essentially groups diverse stimuli into compressed representations: complex states of affairs become remembered as compact biophysical engrams – this is the essence of the kind of modularity when a simple biophysical event kicks off the formation of a complex morphogenetic cascade such as building a “hand” in embryogenesis.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Animal senses use the same ion channel mechanisms found in bacteria
claims.statement: The senses of complex animals (touch, taste, temperature, hearing, etc.) are mediated by the same ion channel mechanisms that bacteria already used to sense their world.
claims.quote: Complex animals’ sense of touch, taste, temperature, hearing, etc. are mediated by the exact same ion channel mechanisms that were already discovered by bacteria and used to make sense of their world (Tasneem et al., 2005; Blackwell, 2006; Liebeskind et al., 2012; Nilius and Honore, 2012).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Cells in development minimize surprise and variational free energy like nervous systems
claims.statement: Living systems minimize surprise and optimize variational free energy by tuning internal states to best predict future stimuli, and this holds for individual cells during metazoan development as much as for nervous systems.
claims.quote: Systems minimize surprise and optimize variational free energy by tuning their internal states in a way that optimally predicts future stimuli (Friston and Ao, 2012; Friston, 2013; Badcock et al., 2019). This is as true for nervous systems as it is for individual cells during metazoan development (Friston et al., 2015; Ramstead et al., 2019).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Multicellularity and morphological complexity are driven by greedy infotaxis
claims.statement: Morphological complexity and multicellularity are proposed to be driven by greedy infotaxis: cells collecting as much information as possible from as far away in space and time as possible to minimize surprise, with greater network connectivity enlarging what the compound individual can sense, remember and store.
claims.quote: It is proposed that morphological complexity and multicellularity are driven by greedy infotaxis (Vergassola et al., 2007) – collecting as much information as possible, from as far away (in both space and time) as possible, to minimize surprise and optimize prediction.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Gap-junction coupling lets cells share sensing and form a larger Self
claims.statement: When cells are coupled into networks by gap junctions, the whole collective can measure and act on the same sensory data, so its Umwelt expands into a larger individual; physiological connectivity is thus the binding mechanism for larger unified Selves.
claims.quote: When coupled into networks via gap junctions however, the whole collective can measure and act upon the same sensory data – the Umwelt expands to create a larger individual in which the comprising cells share a unifying picture of the world (Figure 4).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Most anesthetics in plants and animals are gap junction uncouplers
claims.statement: Most anesthetics that remove cognition and sensory experience, in both plants and animals, act as gap junctional (bioelectric) uncouplers, which the author takes as consistent with connectivity binding cells into larger Selves.
claims.quote: It is thus no coincidence that most anesthetics used to remove cognition and sensory experience, whether in plants or animals, are gap junctional (bioelectric) uncouplers (Mantz et al., 1993; Wentlandt et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2012; Gremiaux et al., 2014; Baluska et al., 2016).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Swarms should show the same cognitive illusions as vertebrate brains
claims.statement: The proposed scale-invariant scaling of cognition predicts that swarm organisms should fall prey to the same kinds of cognitive illusions and failures of rationality as vertebrate brains, which the author says has been observed in ants and slime molds.
claims.quote: A prediction of this proposed scaling is that swarm organisms should fall prey to the same kinds of cognitive illusions and specific failures of rationality as do vertebrate brains, which has indeed been observed in ants and slime molds (Sakiyama and Gunji, 2013, 2016; Tani et al., 2014; Beekman and Latty, 2015).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Selves form only at intermediate levels of information sharing between subunits
claims.statement: Cognitive light cones grow or shrink as an agent's organization changes, and the key is a balance of selective information sharing through "synapses" (any structures that gate signals based on the state of others): too little sharing fails to bind subunits into a new Self, and too much yields an undifferentiated soup without modules or layered abstraction.
claims.quote: Too little sharing results in a failure to bind subunits into a new Self. Too much sharing results in a homogenous soup with insufficient differentiation of modules and abstraction of information across distinct layers.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

claims.label: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of a cell's computational boundary
claims.statement: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of the computational boundary of the Self: by becoming isolated from surrounding tissue's physiological (bioelectric) signals, a cell's cognitive boundary shrinks to its pre-multicellular, single-cell size, so it reverts to proliferating and migrating for its own benefit.
claims.quote: Cancer is a (reversible) shrinking of the computational boundary of a biosystem: by isolating itself from the surrounding tissue’s physiological signals, a cell’s cognitive boundary shrinks to the small size it had before multicellularity.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

claims.label: Agents scaled up from homeostatic loops by adding memory, anticipation and networks
claims.statement: Agents evolved by scaling up from basic homeostatic loops (whose set points are the first goals), driven by surprise minimization, through the successive addition of delays (memory), anticipation (inference), and spatially distributed networks that allow learning and abstraction.
claims.quote: Agents scaled up by evolving from basic homeostatic loops, driven by active inference (surprise minimization) via addition of delays (memory), anticipation (inference), and networks (spatially-distributed processing that enables learning and progressive abstraction/generalization from data).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

claims.label: Morphogenetic goal-directedness smooths the fitness landscape and boosts evolvability
claims.statement: Morphogenetic goal-directedness is a major evolutionary ratchet: because tissues adjust to reach the same anatomical goals despite changed conditions (e.g. muscle, vessels and tendons building a workable extra finger around an ectopic bone), it hides the disruptive effects of random mutations and smooths the anatomical fitness landscape.
claims.quote: Morphogenetic goal-directedness is a major evolutionary ratchet, smoothing the anatomical fitness landscape by hiding the otherwise potentially disruptive effects of random mutations.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Brains are not hardwired: ectopic tail eyes in tadpoles still support vision
claims.statement: Brains, like other developing organs, are not hardwired but can ascertain the body's structure and adjust their programs; tadpoles made to develop eyes on their tails, connected to the spinal cord rather than the brain, can still see quite well.
claims.quote: Tadpoles engineered to develop with eyes on their tails instead of in their usual spot can see quite well, despite the fact that the eyes connect to the spinal cord, not the brain (Blackiston and Levin, 2013; Blackiston et al., 2017). Brains, like other developing organs, are not hardwired but are able to ascertain the structure of the body and adjust their functional programs accordingly
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Editing bioelectric pattern set points can reprogram anatomy without genome editing
claims.statement: A better strategy for regenerative medicine than genetic rewiring of cells may be to edit the pattern-homeostatic set point and let wild-type cells build to it, as shown by altering bioelectric state in planaria to give permanently double-headed worms without genomic editing.
claims.quote: I have previously suggested that a better strategy than cellular re-wiring at the genetic level may be to edit the pattern-homeostatic set point and let wild-type cells build to the new spec. For example, the ability to re-write target morphology in planarian regeneration was recently shown, by altering the bioelectric state in flatworms, without genomic editing, giving rise to permanently double-headed worms (Durant et al., 2017; Levin et al., 2018).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Bioelectric circuits act as software: multistable states switched without genetic change
claims.statement: Ion channel and gap junction circuits are well suited to the "software" of life because they form feedback loops that implement dynamical systems with multiple attractors, which transient signals can switch between without changing the hardware (i.e. without mutating the DNA encoding the channels).
claims.quote: What makes electric circuits, whether ion channel-mediated or electronic, good for software is that they easily implement dynamical systems that have multiple attractors and can be made to occupy one physiological state or another by transient inputs (signals), not requiring changing the hardware (i.e., mutating the DNA encoding that hardware).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Opiate addictiveness may derive from an ancient role in keeping cells together
claims.statement: If multicellularity arose from a drive to minimize predictive error, cells need a way to keep other cells nearby; this suggests the testable hypothesis that the addictive power of opiates and similar molecules derives from such ancient roots, which could be tested in early models of multicellularity and stem/somatic cell co-cultures.
claims.quote: Specifically, the implementation of multicellularity by the drive to minimize predictive error (Fields and Levin, 2019) suggests that cells need a way to keep other cells nearby. This suggests the testable hypothesis that the addictive power of opiates and similar molecules derives from such ancient roots.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

claims.label: Forced electrogenic and gap junction expression could make unicells form bodies
claims.statement: The proposed role of bioelectrics in multicellularity predicts that forcing expression of appropriate electrogenic proteins and gap junctions in a unicellular organism should induce metazoan-like bodies, and that appropriate changes of bioelectric dynamics may dissolve a metazoan body.
claims.quote: The proposed crucial role of bioelectrics in multicellularity predicts that it should be possible to induce the formation of metazoan-like bodies in an otherwise unicellular organism by forcing the expression of appropriate electrogenic proteins and gap junctions. Similarly, it may be possible to induce dissolution of an entire metazoan body by appropriate changes of bioelectric dynamics.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

claims.label: Regeneration across kingdoms should consistently use electrogenic proteins
claims.statement: Bioelectrics should be widely conserved in regeneration across kingdoms: transcriptomes of regeneration from damaged bacterial biofilms to plants to animal limb and organ regeneration should show consistent use of electrogenic proteins, and neurotransmitter signalling should be conserved enough that cognitive-modulator drugs affect biofilms and Physarum.
claims.quote: Bioelectrics should be widely conserved in regeneration across Kingdoms; transcriptomic analyses of regeneration events from damaged bacterial biofilms to plants to metazoan models of limb and organ regeneration should all show consistent use of electrogenic proteins in the events that enable cooperation toward self-limiting morphogenetic cascades.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

claims.label: Cells and tissues may have something it is like to make decisions
claims.statement: Because some nervous systems give rise to first-person experience and neural and non-neural networks differ minimally apart from time scale, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something it is like to be a tissue or organ making decisions, e.g. a pancreas may have as much proto-consciousness as a simple neural network.
claims.quote: But, given that at least some nervous systems do give rise to such experience and that the differences between neural networks and non-neural ones (aside from temporal scale) are minimal, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something-it-is-like to being a tissue or organ and making decisions.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › What Does It Feel Like to be a Pancreas?

claims.label: Evolutionary algorithms can design novel living organisms built from frog cells
claims.statement: A pipeline in which an evolutionary algorithm designs candidate organisms in silico for a desired function, and transferable designs are then built from Xenopus cells with a cell-based construction toolkit, can produce novel living systems that show the predicted behaviours, though some steps still need manual intervention.
claims.quote: Here we show a scalable pipeline for creating functional novel lifeforms: AI methods automatically design diverse candidate lifeforms in silico to perform some desired function, and transferable designs are then created using a cell-based construction toolkit to realize living systems with the predicted behaviors.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Abstract

claims.label: Designed organisms moved as simulated when upright, much less when inverted
claims.statement: For at least one deciliated, cardiac-muscle-powered design, the upright organisms' direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations, and inverting the design significantly reduced net displacement both in silico and in vivo.
claims.quote: More specifically, the upright organisms’ direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations (P < 0.01; details in SI Appendix, section S9), and inverting the design significantly reduced its net displacement both in silico (P < 0.001) and in vivo (P < 0.0001).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Locomotion.

claims.label: Behaviour transfer from simulation to organism was due to the designed shape
claims.statement: The authors interpret the orientation-dependent match between simulated and living organisms as showing that successful transfer of locomotion from simulation to the living organism was due to the designed morphology itself, not chance.
claims.quote: This suggests that successful transference did not result by chance but rather was due to the design itself.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Locomotion.

claims.label: Motile designs spontaneously aggregate particles in simulation and in vivo
claims.statement: When the environment contains particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously gather the particles into aggregates, both in simulation and as living Xenopus-cell organisms.
claims.quote: When the environment is strewn with particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously aggregate the external objects both in silico (SI Appendix, Fig. S10) and in vivo (Fig. 3F and SI Appendix, Fig. S11).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Object Manipulation.

claims.label: Pairs of organisms collide, bond and orbit, more so with cilia active
claims.statement: Collective behaviours predicted in simulation were observed in vivo: two organisms often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond and orbit each other for several revolutions before detaching, and this is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited.
claims.quote: For instance, two designs often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond, and orbit about each other for several revolutions before detaching along tangential trajectories (SI Appendix, Fig. S10). This phenomenon is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited on the organisms
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Collective Behavior.

claims.label: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes
claims.statement: In the voxel-based soft-body simulation with randomly phased contractile cells, selection for locomotion produced morphologies that derandomize motion: shape and the distribution of passive and contractile cells evolved so the global movement was coherent despite random actuation.
claims.quote: As a side effect of selection pressure for locomotion, derandomizing morphologies evolved: evolutionary improvement occurred through changes in overall shape, and distribution of the passive and contractile cells, to collectively derandomize the global movement produced by the random actuation.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

claims.label: Cell competence lets neural-less novel aggregates self-organize functionally
claims.statement: The behavioural competence of individual cells and their propensity to cooperate in groups facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances, so that the designed organisms, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories and mixing tissues, still possess self-organizing properties that support their designed behaviour.
claims.quote: The behavioral competence of individual cells, and the propensity of cells to cooperate in groups, facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances. The lifeforms presented here, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories, and being composed of materials from different tissues, nevertheless possess these self-organizing properties.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

claims.label: Cardiomyocytes in built organisms spontaneously made phase-matched contractions
claims.statement: Although signalling between cardiomyocytes was not designed or enforced, cardiac muscle cells in the built organisms spontaneously coordinated to produce coherent, phase-matched contractions that aided locomotion.
claims.quote: For instance, although signaling between cardiomyocytes was not enforced, emergent spontaneous coordination among the cardiac muscle cells produced coherent, phase-matched contractions which aided locomotion in the physically realized designs.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

claims.label: Reconfigurable organisms self-repair, closing lacerations
claims.statement: Reconfigurable organisms built from Xenopus cells maintain their externally imposed shape and also self-repair after damage, for example automatically closing lacerations.
claims.quote: Finally, reconfigurable organisms not only self-maintain their externally imposed configuration, but they also self-repair in the face of damage, such as automatically closing lacerations (SI Appendix, Fig. S9).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

claims.label: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones
claims.statement: Designs first evolved on simulated land had bounding gaits that did not transfer to living organisms; adding first-order hydrodynamics and randomized phase offsets produced designs whose behaviour better matched the living systems, in contact with the ground for 93.3% of evaluation versus 52.7% on the first pass.
claims.quote: The behavior of designs generated on the second pass better matched the behavior of the actual living systems: on average, designs were in contact with the ground plane for 93.3% of their evaluation period, compared to just 52.7% on the first pass (SI Appendix, section S6).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
