claims.label: Information flows first from the anatomical loop to single-cell energy
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy from energy to cell state peaks before the reverse flow, indicating that information is first driven by the tissue-level anatomical homeostatic loop, which then controls the energy cells need to survive; the authors take this to suggest top-down information is key to manipulating tissue dynamics.
claims.quote: Thus, in our scheme, the information was first driven by the anatomical loop, and the energy needed for single-cell survival was controlled by this loop.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Stress rises when cellular memory fails to predict the future
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, stress increases concurrently with a fall in local active information storage of cell states, so evolution used the stress system as a communication channel activated when memory of past events does not predict the future, matching the definition of stressors as unpredictable or uncontrollable stimuli.
claims.quote: In our scheme, evolution used the stress system as a communication system that was activated when memory of past events was not effective for predicting the future.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Model predicts sudden late remodelling of apparently stable biological patterns
claims.statement: Because the neural cellular automaton suddenly remodelled cell fates after a long period of quiescent, stable pattern, the authors predict that something similar may occur in biological systems: some phenotypes that appear complete may need to be followed much longer to see their true dynamics.
claims.quote: The sudden remodelling of cell fates after a long period of apparently quiescent, stable pattern in our model (figure 4) predicts that something similar may occur in biological systems.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Experimental results on repatterning of planaria

claims.label: 22% of headless ERK-inhibited planaria spontaneously repattern weeks later
claims.statement: In Dugesia japonica made headless by transient U0126 (ERK/MAP kinase inhibitor) treatment after amputation, 22% of 181 animals followed until death showed sudden repatterning after four or more weeks without any intervention, mostly between 4 and 10 weeks, and 61% of those regained a normal single-headed morphology.
claims.quote: In headless animals observed from when they were cut until their death (n = 181), 22% showed some form of sudden repatterning even though regeneration had completed and morphogenesis had ceased weeks prior (figure 10b).
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Experimental results on repatterning of planaria

claims.label: Planarian tissues have processes operating far slower than known regeneration
claims.statement: The spontaneous restoration of normal morphology in headless planaria many weeks after regeneration has completed suggests that planarian tissues contain processes operating on a time scale much longer than previously known.
claims.quote: This spontaneous repatterning that allows the re-establishment of a normal morphology many weeks after regeneration is completed suggests the existence of tissue processes that operate on a time scale much longer than previously known.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Experimental results on repatterning of planaria

claims.label: Evolved tissues show delayed gratification as an unselected free lunch
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, the tissue temporarily moves away from its target pattern to remove misplaced cells and then returns (delayed gratification in the TAME framework), and since neither this nor long-term maintenance was selected for, such capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems can emerge as a 'free lunch' without direct selection.
claims.quote: Interestingly, neither of these things were directly selected for during the evolutionary cycle, revealing how some capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems can emerge as a kind of ‘free lunch’, without direct selection pressure [2,88].
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

claims.label: Regeneration can start without injury, so a missing-tissue response may be unnecessary
claims.statement: Because headless planaria mounted a regenerative response with no triggering injury, the authors argue this is consistent with the idea that a missing-tissue response may not be necessary for regeneration and that subtle internal dynamics may suffice to initiate change long after a process seems to have stabilized.
claims.quote: The newly demonstrated ability to mount a regenerative response without any triggering injury is consistent with the idea that a MTR may not be necessary for regeneration to occur [90] and that subtle internal dynamics may be sufficient to initiate change long after the process appears to have reached a stable point.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

claims.label: Stress-driven spatial patterning may be conserved across bacteria, metazoa and models
claims.statement: Noting that oscillatory nitrogen stress responses pattern bacterial biofilms and that stress responses define stripe regions in their simulated tissue, the authors suggest that conserved stress-based dynamics could underlie the scaling of spatial patterning from single-cell metabolic goals in bacteria, metazoans and minimal in silico models, similar to the clock-and-wavefront model of somitogenesis.
claims.quote: Thus, conserved dynamics could be relevant across bacterial, metazoan and in silico minimal models of the scaling of spatial patterning from single-cell metabolic and stress dynamics.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

claims.label: Somatic cells kept their cognitive repertoire and scaled it to anatomical goals
claims.statement: The authors argue that somatic cells did not lose their ancestral cognitive and computational capabilities when they became part of multicellular bodies, but scaled them up to pursue larger anatomical goals.
claims.quote: But somatic cells did not lose their cognitive repertoire and computational capabilities during their transitions to multicellularity or in becoming part of metazoan swarms (bodies): they scaled them to pursue larger anatomical goals [4].
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

claims.label: Evolution pivoted cellular collective intelligence into behavioural intelligence
claims.statement: The authors propose that evolution turned the collective intelligence of cells during body morphogenesis into traditional behavioural intelligence by scaling up the goals (homeostatic setpoints) at the centre of homeostatic processes, so that body patterning and cognition lie on one continuum.
claims.quote: We propose that evolution pivoted the collective intelligence of cells during morphogenesis of the body into traditional behavioural intelligence by scaling up the goals at the centre of homeostatic processes.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

claims.label: Irreversibility of morphogenesis, not Weismann's barrier, is what limits Lamarckism
claims.statement: Because morphogenesis is a recursive, highly emergent process, the inverse problem of determining which genomic changes would produce a desired large-scale anatomical feature is in general unsolvable, and this irreversibility, rather than any inability to edit the germline in light of somatic experience, is what limits full-scale Lamarckian inheritance.
claims.quote: This irreversibility of the recursive, highly emergent process of morphogenesis is what limits full-scale Lamarckism: the difficulty is not how to penetrate Weismann’s barrier and edit the genome in light of somatic experience—mechanisms exist for this [21–23].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › From genotype to phenotype in development: implications of an indirect pathway

claims.label: Evolution searches the space of behaviour-shaping signals rather than local rules
claims.statement: Because metazoan cells are agential (they retain adaptive behaviours from unicellular ancestors), what evolution mainly searches is not the enormous space of all possible local rules but the space of behaviour-shaping signals by which cells hack each other's functionality, and the collective intelligence of cell swarms strongly affects the rate and course of evolution.
claims.quote: I argue that what evolution is really searching is not the enormous space of all possible local rules, but instead the space of behavior-shaping signals by which cells hack each other’s functionality, and that the collective intelligence [38, 39] of cellular swarms has major implications for the rate and course of evolution.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › From genotype to phenotype in development: implications of an indirect pathway

claims.label: A generative, compressed genome pushes evolution toward general-purpose problem solvers
claims.statement: By using an architecture akin to a variational autoencoder, in which the genome is a compressed generative representation decoded by the developmental layer, evolution is kept from over-training on past conditions and is pushed to produce general-purpose problem-solving organisms that display robustness, plasticity and adaptive success in entirely novel circumstances.
claims.quote: Second is that by using a variational autoencoder-like architecture of compression into a generative genome (Fig. 1), evolution is freed from over-training on past conditions and pushed to evolve general-purpose problem-solving machines which inevitably display robustness, plasticity, and adaptive success in entirely novel circumstances.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Intelligence and evolution: the impact of competency at new scales

claims.label: Gap-junction coupling scales cell competencies into larger collective goal states
claims.statement: Basal cellular competencies were not lost in the transition to multicellularity but scaled up into collective intelligence; gap-junctional merging of intracellular milieus and other tissue-level signalling (e.g. stress propagation) share chemical engrams, erase the individuality of cells, and enlarge the memory, predictive capacity and sensory/effector radius of cell networks so they can pursue larger goal states such as anatomical targets.
claims.quote: This promotes sharing of chemical engrams, which also help to wipe the individuality of cells, and enlarges the memory, predictive capacity, and sensory/effector radius of cellular networks, enabling them to pursue larger goal states in spaces like anatomical morphospace [14].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Scaling up from cellular competency to collective intelligence

claims.label: Freed from embryonic signals, frog skin cells form self-motile Xenobots
claims.statement: Frog (Xenopus) embryonic epithelial cells, which in vivo form a passive protective outer layer, instead form Xenobots (functional, self-motile constructs with novel behaviours) when liberated from the instructive influences of other cells, showing that such behaviours are normally suppressed by signalling from neighbouring cells during development.
claims.quote: However, when liberated from the instructive influences of the other cells, frog epithelial cells instead form a Xenobot—a functional, self-motile construct with many novel behaviors that are normally suppressed and hidden by the instructive signaling of other cells during development [125].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Scaling up from cellular competency to collective intelligence

claims.label: Bioelectric networks were exploited for information integration since bacterial biofilms
claims.statement: Evolution discovered very early, around the time of bacterial biofilms, that electrical networks of ion channels and pumps are a convenient way to integrate and process information across space and time and to scale the functions of individual cells toward large-scale tasks, the same reason brains use this modality.
claims.quote: But evolution discovered very early on, around the time of bacterial biofilms [144], that electric networks are also extremely convenient ways to integrate and process information across space and time, and to scale the functions of individual computing units towards a large-scale task (the same reason that brains, and computers, use this modality [145]).
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric control: a mechanism for scaling cell behaviors to large-scale morphogenetic goals

claims.label: Reproducing face bioelectric patterns via ion-channel misexpression induces ectopic eyes
claims.statement: The vertebrate face is patterned by bioelectric gradients that regionalize gene expression, and reproducing these voltage patterns elsewhere in a tadpole by misexpressing specific ion channels induces whole ectopic organs such as eyes on the gut or tail, regions not otherwise competent to make eyes in response to Pax6.
claims.quote: Reproducing these patterns elsewhere in the body via misexpression of specific ion channels enables the induction of whole ectopic organs, such as eyes [152] on the gut or tail of a tadpole (thus unlocking novel capabilities of body regions, since only the anterior neurectoderm is competent to make eyes via signals from the chemical master regulator Pax6).
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric control: a mechanism for scaling cell behaviors to large-scale morphogenetic goals

claims.label: Tadpoles see through an ectopic tail eye without generations of adaptation
claims.statement: Tadpoles whose native eyes are prevented from forming and which carry an ectopic eye on the tail can see and perform well in visual behavioural training even though that eye connects to the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain, so a radical change to sensory–motor architecture yields successful behaviour without generations of adaptation.
claims.quote: Tadpoles, in which the native eyes are prevented from forming and an ectopic eye is instead placed on the tail, can see and perform well in visual behavioral training [176], even though the ectopic eye connects to the spinal cord (or just to peripheral tissue) rather than to the brain—this radical change to the sensory–motor architecture does not require generations of adaptation to produce successful behavior.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Morphogenetic control as a collective intelligence

claims.label: Polyploid newt kidney tubules are built by one giant cell instead of eight to ten
claims.statement: In polyploid newts, whose cells are enlarged by extra genome copies, kidney tubules normally made by eight to ten communicating cells are instead formed by a single enormous cell wrapping around itself, so a different molecular mechanism (cytoskeletal bending rather than cell–cell communication) is deployed to reach the same anatomical outcome, an instance of downward causation in the service of a large-scale anatomical goal.
claims.quote: In the kidney system of polyploid newts, the normal cell:cell communication that creates a tubule from eight to ten cells working together is swapped for a single enormous cell that wraps around itself to create the same final outcome [184].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Morphogenetic control as a collective intelligence

claims.label: Bioelectric patterns act as hidden layers that split the genotype–anatomy inverse problem
claims.statement: Bioelectric networks mitigate the inverse problem of morphogenesis by acting as 'hidden layers' between genetics and anatomy: the mapping from ion channel genes to bioelectric pattern, and from bioelectric pattern to anatomy, are each easier to invert than the direct genotype–anatomy map, decomposing the control problem into two easier ones for evolution and for engineers.
claims.quote: The relationships of ion channel genes to the bioelectric pattern, and bioelectric pattern to its resulting anatomy, are each easier to invert than the direct genotype–anatomy link, so they help to decompose the control problem into two easier problems.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

claims.label: Voltage is the instructive variable: an unrelated yeast pump can replace tail V-ATPase
claims.statement: Membrane voltage is a coarse-grained, high-order parameter over ion channel and pump microstates: electrogenic proteins can be swapped as long as the bioelectric state is correct, e.g. the V-ATPase function in tadpole tail regeneration can be phenocopied by a yeast proton pump with no sequence or structural homology.
claims.quote: electrogenic proteins can be swapped out as needed (e.g., V-ATPase complex in the tadpole tail can be phenocopied by a yeast proton pump with no sequence or structural homology, because it produces the correct physiological signal), and everything still works as long as the bioelectric state is correct [190].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

claims.label: Genetically wild-type planarian cells can store more than one target morphology
claims.statement: In planaria, a brief (2-day) physiological intervention can reset the bioelectric circuit that controls head number from the default one-head pattern memory to a two-head pattern, so the same genetically wild-type cells can harbour multiple bioelectrically encoded target morphologies that guide regeneration.
claims.quote: In this case, the exact same hardware (genetically wild-type planarian cells) can harbor multiple representations of the bioelectrically encoded target morphology that guides the cellular collectives during regeneration [193–195].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

claims.label: Bioelectric changes let wild-type planaria grow other species' head shapes in days
claims.statement: Head shapes of existing planarian species are readily recapitulated by genetically wild-type planaria whose bioelectric circuit is altered during regeneration, so 100–150 million years of evolutionary distance in morphospace can be crossed in a few days through the dynamics of bioelectric pattern memories.
claims.quote: Indeed, it has been shown that existing planarian species’ head shapes are readily recapitulated by a genetically wild-type animal experiencing changes to its bioelectric circuit during regeneration—100–150 million years of evolutionary distance in morphospace can be crossed in a few days because of the dynamics of bioelectric pattern memories [197, 198].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

claims.label: Surgically altered ciliate cortex is inherited across generations despite wild-type DNA
claims.statement: In unicellular ciliates, changes made to cell-surface form can be inherited across generations independently of DNA: surgical rotation of a small patch of cortex creates a stable line in which part of the ciliary beat pushes food out of the mouth, which the wild-type genome cannot correct.
claims.quote: Changes made to unicellular form can persist across generations [203–205]; for example, surgical rotation of a small patch of the cell surface creates a stable line of animals in which a portion of the ciliary beat pushes food out of their mouths—a condition which their perfectly wild-type genome cannot correct.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales

claims.label: Planaria adapt to barium by changing expression of only a handful of genes
claims.statement: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker that is evolutionarily novel to them, first lose their heads but then regrow barium-insensitive heads, with only a handful of genes up- or down-regulated, showing that cells can navigate transcriptional space to solve a problem for which there was no selection.
claims.quote: Transcriptional analysis reveals that these tissues up- and down-regulate just a handful of genes to get back to physiological and anatomical setpoints despite the inability to regulate potassium.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales

claims.label: Animals with robust regeneration also resist cancer and aging
claims.statement: Animals with robust morphogenetic control due to high plasticity are resistant to perturbation at many scales: they regenerate lost limbs and organs, readily suppress cancer, and resist aging, contrary to the expectation that easy access to undifferentiated cells should make them highly cancer-prone.
claims.quote: Animals with robust morphogenetic control due to high levels of plasticity are resistant to changes of circumstance (injury) at many scales: they regenerate after loss of limbs and organs (degradation of body-scale information), they suppress cancer readily [238] (degradation of tissue-scale information) and they resist aging (degradation of cell-level information).
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Beginner’s mind: self-organization on the fly as the origin of multiscale competency

claims.label: Competency gains drive a ratchet toward ever greater multiscale competency
claims.statement: Because each gain in developmental competency makes the structural genome harder for selection to evaluate, evolution increasingly optimizes the competency mechanisms themselves, a feedback ratchet for multiscale intelligence that appears in computational models and has run to different extents in planaria, salamanders and mammals.
claims.quote: This starts a feedback loop, because each gain in competency makes it even harder to judge the structural genome, which exacerbates the drive toward improving competencies—a ratchet for multiscale intelligence that can readily be seen in computational models of the process [240].
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › An evolutionary intelligence ratchet

claims.label: The competency ratchet predicts no planarian mutant strains with abnormal morphology
claims.statement: The competency-ratchet model predicts, and it is the case, that there are no known mutant planarian strains with abnormal morphologies (unlike flies or mice), explains the difficulty of making transgenic planaria, and the only known permanent abnormal planarian lines (two-headed and randomized 1- vs 2-head forms) arose from bioelectric rather than genetic change.
claims.quote: For example, it predicts the confirmed fact that there are no known mutant planarian strains with abnormal morphologies (the way there are for fruit flies, mice, etc.) and explains why the research community has had such a hard time (despite decades of efforts) generating transgenic planaria.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › An evolutionary intelligence ratchet

claims.label: Multiscale competency smooths the fitness landscape and lets search escape local maxima
claims.statement: The multiscale competency architecture smooths the fitness landscape by reducing phenotypic differences between genotypes, letting evolution explore mutations that would otherwise be lethal (e.g. a mutation that displaces the mouth but has another benefit survives because the mouth self-corrects), which makes search more efficient and helps it overcome local maxima.
claims.quote: By smoothing the fitness landscape, MCA makes the search process much more efficient, improving evolvability by enabling the search to overcome local maxima.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Implications of multiscale competency for the evolutionary process

claims.label: Developmental error-correction makes mutations neutral and builds up cryptic variation
claims.statement: By buffering mutational effects through developmental regulation, the multiscale competency architecture makes neutral many mutations that would be deleterious under a direct genotype-to-phenotype mapping, so they persist as a pool of phenotypically dormant cryptic variation that can later be exploited.
claims.quote: MCA makes many mutations neutral that would be deleterious in a direct genotype → phenotype architecture. Such mutations whose effects are mitigated by developmental regulation are not weeded out; instead, they persist, generating over time a rich pool of diversity that may be phenotypically dormant, but can be exploited in future.
claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Implications of multiscale competency for the evolutionary process

claims.label: Physarum learns and decides without neurons, and its behaviour is its morphological change
claims.statement: The unicellular slime mould Physarum learns from repeated experience and makes decisions (e.g. growing towards the heavier of distant inert objects) without a brain, neurons or cellularization, and in Physarum behaviour is implemented as change of body shape, blurring the distinction between morphological and behavioural problems.
claims.quote: These examples of learning and decision-making occur in the absence of a brain, neurons, or cellularization. From the perspective of evolutionary change across behavioral domains, one interesting thing is that for Physarum, its behavior is its morphological change.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change

claims.label: Planarian tail fragments regenerate brains that recall trained behaviour
claims.statement: Tail fragments of planarian flatworms trained on specific tasks regenerate into animals that show recall of the trained information, so behavioural memories are apparently imprinted onto the new brain as it forms, linking the information processing that restores body shape with that which preserves past experience.
claims.quote: Tails of worms trained on specific tasks regenerate into animals that show recall of the original information: the behavioral memories are apparently also imprinted onto the new brain as it forms (McConnell et al. 1959; Shomrat and Levin 2013).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change

claims.label: Xenopus tadpoles with only a tail eye can see through it
claims.statement: Xenopus laevis tadpoles produced with no primary eyes and a single eye on the tail can see out of the ectopic eye, which can connect to the spinal cord, showing that a frog's cellular hardware can adapt within one generation to a radical reconfiguration of its visual system.
claims.quote: Tadpoles of the frog Xenopus laevis can be produced with no primary eyes, but one eye on their tails; these animals can see out of an ectopic eye, which can connect to the spinal cord (Blackiston and Levin 2013).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change

claims.label: Bioelectric network information cannot be read from transcript or protein levels
claims.statement: Because ion channels open and close post-translationally, the same channels can yield different voltage states depending on cell history and different channels can yield the same voltage map, the information content of a bioelectric network cannot be read out at the transcriptional or proteomic level and must be studied in living tissue.
claims.quote: As a corollary, the information content of this network cannot be read out at the transcriptional or even proteomic level: channels open and close post-translationally, and the same channels can give rise to different voltage states depending on cells’ history, while diverse channels can give rise to the exact same voltage map.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue

claims.label: Bioelectric networks are a cognitive glue that enlarges the cognitive light cone of cells
claims.statement: Bioelectric networks, through their plasticity, multiscale historicity (memory) and learning capacity, act as a 'cognitive glue' that binds the cybernetic goal-directedness of single cells into a higher-order system pursuing larger-scale goals (a larger cognitive light cone), and this capacity is not unique to brains.
claims.quote: Bioelectric networks, with their inherent plasticity, multiscale historicity, and learning capacity, are an ideal kind of “cognitive glue” that binds the primitive goal-directedness (in the cybernetic sense) of single cells into a higher order system with a larger cognitive light cone (Fig. 1E).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue

claims.label: Neural bioelectric machinery was an evolutionary pivot from navigating morphospace
claims.statement: Ion channels, gap junctions and neurotransmitters were originally used to control cell behaviours toward morphogenetic outcomes (navigating anatomical morphospace); their use to drive 3D behaviour via muscle is an evolutionary pivot, exapted with a speed-up from hours to milliseconds and a shift from spatial to temporal (spiking) patterns, and this conservation is why neuroscience tools work throughout the body.
claims.quote: The current use of these components to implement behaviors in 3D space by controlling muscle activity represents an evolutionary pivot: their original usage was to navigate anatomical morphospace (Fields et al. 2020) (that is, to control all cell behaviors toward specific morphogenetic outcomes).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue

claims.label: Morphogenetic pattern memory habituates: repeatedly amputated axolotl limbs stop regrowing
claims.statement: The anatomical setpoint that guides regeneration is a pattern memory that is stable but modifiable by experience; for example, repeated amputation of axolotl limbs leads the tissue to habituate to the loss and eventually stop trying to regrow.
claims.quote: This pattern memory can, like any good memory, be modified by experience (it is stable, but also labile to the right kinds of stimuli). For example, repeated amputation of axolotl limbs leads to the tissue habituating to the loss of limb and eventually giving up trying to re-grow (Bryant et al. 2017).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Memory and target morphology

claims.label: Deer antlers re-form an ectopic branch at a past injury site year after year
claims.statement: In deer trophic memory, an ectopic branch is formed in the otherwise stereotyped antler at the location of earlier damage year after year, long after the damaged rack has been shed, a memory of 3D position held by scalp cells that regenerate the antler annually.
claims.quote: Trophic memory in deer (Bubenik and Pavlansky 1965; Lobo et al. 2014) enables an ectopic branch in their otherwise stereotypical antler structure to be formed year after year, at a specific point of earlier damage, long after the damaged antler rack has been shed
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Memory and target morphology

claims.label: Bioelectrically induced two-headed planaria stay two-headed across later regenerations
claims.statement: In planarian flatworms the number of heads a regenerating fragment builds is set by the state of a bioelectric circuit with a default of one; transiently modifying it re-sets it to 'two', and the resulting two-headed worms keep regenerating as two-headed through multiple rounds of cutting without further manipulation, unless the pattern is experimentally reset.
claims.quote: Remarkably, when cut again in multiple subsequent rounds of regeneration (with no further manipulation), the fragments continue to result in two-headed animals. This shift in the target morphology for regeneration is permanent (unless the animal’s bioelectric pattern memory is reset back to a one-headed state by an experimental manipulation).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales

claims.label: Planarian head number is not directly encoded in the genome
claims.statement: How many heads a planarian cellular collective produces is not directly encoded in its genome, since the same wild-type cells can produce 1-, 2- or 0-headed planaria depending on their history; the genome encodes the hardware (e.g. ion channels) while the outcome results from experience-sensitive electrophysiological 'software'.
claims.quote: The question, of how many heads a given cellular collective will produce, is, surprisingly, not directly encoded in its genome because exactly the same, wild-type set of cells can produce 1-, 2-, or 0-headed planaria depending on their history.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales

claims.label: Genetic assimilation of bioelectric phenotypes likely shaped body-plan evolution
claims.statement: Evolutionary changes in ion channel properties that lead to genetic assimilation of bioelectrically induced phenotypes are likely an important aspect of the evolution of body plans and other morphological features, analogous to the Baldwin effect for learning.
claims.quote: Evolutionary tweaks of ion channel properties that eventually lead to genetic assimilation of bioelectrically induced phenotypes is likely an important aspect of the evolution of body plans and other morphological features, much as the Baldwin effect is thought to be a key dynamic for the role of cognition and learning in evolutionary lineages (Baldwin 1896).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales

claims.label: Commensal bacteria can hijack planarian morphogenesis to cause two-headed regeneration
claims.statement: Like parasites that manipulate host neurobehavioural systems, commensal bacteria can override the default planarian morphogenetic control system and cause two-headed regeneration.
claims.quote: the planarian morphogenetic control system too can be hijacked not only by bioengineers (as described above) but also by commensal bacteria which can over-ride the default system and lead to two-headed regeneration (Williams et al. 2020).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation

claims.label: A latent two-head bioelectric pattern is a counterfactual memory of the future target form
claims.statement: Because a two-headed bioelectric pattern can exist in an anatomically normal one-headed planarian with normal gene expression, the bioelectric pattern is not a readout of current anatomy but a representation of the target morphology to be built if the animal is injured, in effect a counterfactual memory.
claims.quote: In the case of a two-headed pattern in a one-headed host, this means that the bioelectrical pattern is not a read-out of what the anatomy is currently, but rather a representation of what it should be, weeks later, following regeneration if the animal is injured.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation

claims.label: Ion channel drugs can make planarian head number flip stochastically at each regeneration
claims.statement: Exposure to ion channel drugs can put the planarian bioelectric circuit into a bistable state in which, at each regeneration, fragments of these 'cryptic' worms randomly regenerate as one-headed or two-headed, analogous to bistability in perceptual systems.
claims.quote: Exposure to ion channel drugs (a physiological experience akin to electrical signals from a retina or other sense organ, not a genetic change) can place the bioelectric circuit into a state in which it cannot decide between two outcomes and flips back and forth stochastically at each regenerative event (recall of target morphology).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation

claims.label: Transient gap-junction blockade makes planarian fragments build heads of other species
claims.statement: Temporary exposure of planarian fragments to a blocker of electrical synapses (gap junctions) causes them to build head shapes of other planarian species 100–150 million years distant, with no genetic change; Levin interprets this as the bioelectric network navigating to other attractors in morphospace, and the worms later remodel back to normal.
claims.quote: One example of this plasticity of morphogenetic behavior (expanding on the default genetically encoded repertoire) is the fact that temporary exposure to a blocker of electrical synapses (i.e., an anesthetic) causes planarian fragments to create the heads of other species, with no genetic change required (Emmons-Bell et al. 2015; Sullivan et al. 2016).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity

claims.label: Newt kidney tubules keep normal diameter with fewer, larger cells, down to one cell
claims.statement: In newts whose embryonic cells are made larger (e.g. by polyploidy), kidney tubules use fewer cells to keep the normal tubule diameter and body size, and with enormous cells a single cell bends around itself to form the tubule, showing that different molecular mechanisms are called on to reach the same large-scale anatomical goal.
claims.quote: However, if the cells of the early embryo are artificially made to be larger, fewer cells will be used, resulting in the same (normal) tubule diameter and overall body size. Remarkably, this can be pushed to a fascinating extreme: if the cells are made to be enormous, a single cell will bend around itself, producing the normal size tubule diameter.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity

claims.label: Xenobots perform kinematic self-replication not known in any other species
claims.statement: Xenobots, proto-organisms that form spontaneously from dissociated frog embryo skin cells, are motile via cilia and perform kinematic self-replication, building copies of themselves from loose cells in the medium, a novel solution reached within 48 h without any evolutionary history of selection as Xenobots.
claims.quote: The most remarkable novel behavior is that of kinematic self-replication: Xenobots build copies of themselves by rearranging loose cells provided to them in the medium. This is Von Neumann-style replication that is not, to our knowledge, used by any other species on Earth.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity

claims.label: Scrambled Xenopus tadpole faces reach a normal frog face by new paths
claims.statement: During metamorphosis, Xenopus laevis tadpoles reach the correct frog face configuration not only from a normal tadpole configuration but also from a wide range of experimentally scrambled craniofacial configurations, using new paths through morphospace that end in the same goal region.
claims.quote: For example, during metamorphosis, the tadpole of Xenopus laevis can reach the correct frog face region of morphospace not only from its default starting position (a normal tadpole configuration), but also from a wide range of scrambled configurations (Vandenberg et al. 2012)—using new paths through that morphospace that nevertheless end up in the same goal region (Friston et al. 2015; Pezzulo and Levin 2016).
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Navigation: an invariant between morphological, behavioral, and other spaces

claims.label: A few bioelectrically induced lens cells recruit host cells to build a normal-sized lens
claims.statement: When an ectopic lens is induced in tail tissue by bioelectric modulation, misexpressing the ion channel in only a small subset of the needed cells suffices: these cells recruit unmodified host cells to reach the critical mass for a normal-sized lens, so downstream modules such as size control are activated without micromanagement.
claims.quote: For example, when an ectopic lens (in tail tissue) is induced by bioelectric modulation, it is sufficient to misexpress the channel only in a small subset of the needed cells: once their organ-level goal is specified, these cells will secondarily recruit other (un-modified) host cells as needed to achieve the critical mass needed to produce a normal-sized lens.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Navigation: an invariant between morphological, behavioral, and other spaces

claims.label: Gap junctions wipe ownership of memory molecules, partly erasing cell individuality
claims.statement: By directly connecting the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells, gap junctions provide an 'owner wiping property' for stress signals and other molecular traces of experience (e.g. calcium flux), so cells cannot tell whether such a signal is their own or a neighbour's; this partly erases individual cell identity and lets the collective scale up measurements, stored goals and actions.
claims.quote: Second, by providing direct connections between the intracellular milieus of cells, they provide an “owner wiping property” for stress signals and other molecular traces of experience: cells cannot tell whether a given memory molecule (e.g., calcium flux) belongs to itself or its neighbors.
claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › E pluribus unum

claims.label: Single adult human lung cells self-construct into motile multicellular biobots
claims.statement: A single normal human bronchial epithelial cell from adult lung, cultured in extracellular matrix for two weeks and then transferred to a low-viscosity medium, self-constructs into a multicellular, motile spheroid (an Anthrobot) without genetic editing, scaffolds or manual sculpting.
claims.quote: Each Anthrobot begins as a single cell, derived from the adult human lung, and self‐constructs into a multicellular motile biobot after being cultured in extra cellular matrix for 2 weeks and transferred into a minimally viscous habitat.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Abstract

claims.label: Morphogenetic plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells
claims.statement: The ability of adult, somatic, genetically wild-type human cells to form a novel functional anatomy with new behaviours shows that the plasticity seen in Xenobots is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells, and is a fundamental feature of wild-type cells that needs no direct genetic manipulation to unlock.
claims.quote: The ability of adult, somatic, human cells to form a novel functional anatomy, with unique behaviors, reveals that this plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cell properties, and is a fundamental feature of wild‐type cells that requires no direct genetic manipulation to unlock.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Introduction

claims.label: Lower viscosity may drive apical-out polarity reversal of airway spheroids
claims.statement: The authors hypothesize that airway spheroids keep cilia in the lumen because basal cells interact with the surrounding high-viscosity matrix, and that moving spheroids to a lower-viscosity, water-based medium may trigger basal cells to migrate inward so the ciliated apical layer takes their place on the spheroid surface.
claims.quote: Given that cilia naturally localize into the lumen due to the basal cells’ interaction with the surrounding high‐viscosity matrix, we hypothesized that changing the culture environment to a lower viscosity level (e.g., water‐based media instead of gel‐based matrix) may trigger the basal layer cells to migrate inward and allow the apical layer to take their place on the spheroid cortex.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

claims.label: Apical-in spheroids become motile within a week in low-adhesive liquid culture
claims.statement: Human bronchial epithelial spheroids that are apical-in and non-motile on release from Matrigel become motile by day 7 in low-adhesive liquid culture, with beating cilia on their outer surface; immunostaining shows a large increase in external multiciliated cells between day 0 and day 7.
claims.quote: This new approach has enabled the originally apical‐in spheroids (that show no motility on day 0 as shown on Figure 1b.1) to became motile by day 7 (Figure 1b.2), featuring highly motile ciliary appendages on the spheroid surface.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

claims.label: Higher culture viscosity reduces Anthrobot motility and size
claims.statement: Culturing Anthrobots in environments more viscous than the protocol baseline decreases both their motility and their size, suggesting that low-viscosity environments favour the growth of functional, larger bots.
claims.quote: We observed that culture environments with higher viscosity levels than the protocol baseline result in decreased motility (Figure S2, Supporting Information) and size (Figure S3, Supporting Information), suggesting that low‐viscosity environments better facilitate the growth of functional bots as well as yield larger bots.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

claims.label: Initial cell seeding density is a control knob for Anthrobot size and maturation
claims.statement: Changing the initial seeding density of bronchial epithelial cells in Matrigel (half, default or double 30,000 cells/mL) significantly changes the resulting Anthrobot sizes and the time course of motility, though not linearly, suggesting that seeding density is a tractable control parameter for Anthrobot morphology and function.
claims.quote: These results show that the size and time course of maturation of motile bots could be modulated by altering the concentration of cells in the Anthrobot differentiation culture, suggesting initial cell seeding density to be a tractable control knob for Anthrobot morphology and function.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

claims.label: Anthrobot motility onset follows a sigmoidal time course peaking around day 10
claims.statement: After release from the matrix, the number of motile Anthrobots rises along a sigmoidal curve over three weeks, with the largest change in motility on day 10, and this rise reflects a morphological reorganization that exposes cilia on the surface.
claims.quote: To characterize the temporal dynamics of motility initiation, we periodically (every other day) counted the number of motile spheroids for 3 weeks following dissolution and observed a sigmoidal motility profile with peak change in motility on day 10 (Figure 1C).
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

claims.label: Anthrobot motility is cilia-driven
claims.statement: Blocking ciliary motion with ciliobrevin sharply decreases Anthrobot motility, showing that their locomotion is driven by surface cilia.
claims.quote: We administered the efficient blocker of cilia motion, ciliobrevin,[ 20 ] and observed the expected drastic decrease in motility (See Figure S6, Supporting Information), confirming that the motility of Anthrobots is cilia‐driven.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

claims.label: Anthrobot trajectories fall into four movement types
claims.statement: Unsupervised clustering of 30-second trajectory segments from about 200 Anthrobots, described by straightness and gyration indices, yields four statistically distinct movement types: circular, linear, curvilinear and eclectic.
claims.quote: Further investigation of these clusters reveals that each represents a distinct movement type: circular, linear, curvilinear and “eclectic” (Figure 2D).
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types

claims.label: Circular motion is the most stable Anthrobot behaviour; eclectic motion is transient
claims.statement: In a Markov-chain model of transitions between movement types, circular motion is the most persistent Anthrobot behaviour, followed by linear and curvilinear motion, while eclectic motion acts as a transient intermediate that probabilistically resolves into one of the other three types.
claims.quote: We observed that the most stable movement pattern for an Anthrobot is circular motion, followed by linear/curvilinear motion. The eclectics act more like an intermediate and over time, at least probabilistically, resolve into one of the 3 other categories.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types

claims.label: Anthrobots self-organize into discrete, stable movement types with individual fingerprints
claims.statement: Because Anthrobot movement types are highly consistent and rarely interconvert (for example between circular and linear), the authors conclude that Anthrobots self-organize into discrete, stable movement types, each bot having a distinct motility fingerprint.
claims.quote: The fact that Anthrobots exhibit movement types with high “consistency” and low rates of inter‐type conversion (e.g., between circulars and linear) suggests that Anthrobots self‐organize into discrete and stable movement types, each bot having a distinct motility fingerprint.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types

claims.label: Morphotype 2 is most ciliated; morphotype 3 has the most polarized cilia
claims.statement: Among the three Anthrobot morphotypes, morphotype 2 (the largest and least regular) is significantly more ciliated than the other two, and morphotype 3 has a significantly more polarized, clustered cilia distribution with the fewest isolated cilia patches.
claims.quote: These four indices together describe type 2 bots as being significantly more ciliated than type 1 and type 3 bots, and type 3 bots as having a significantly more polarized cilia distribution pattern (with the least amount of extra‐cluster noise) in comparison to type 1 and type 2 bots (Figure 3D).
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types

claims.label: Anthrobots form three morphotypes, split first by size and shape, then by cilia pattern
claims.statement: Principal component analysis and clustering of eight shape and cilia indices from about 350 Anthrobots yields three morphotypes, organized as a decision tree in which size and shape smoothness separate small, smooth spherical bots (morphotype 1) from larger, irregular bots, which are then split by cilia pattern into non-polarized (morphotype 2) and polarized (morphotype 3).
claims.quote: In summary, our morphological characterization pipeline suggest that Anthrobots self‐organize into 3 major morphotypes (Figure 3E) and this relationship can be represented by a developmental decision tree shown on Figure 3F wherein the first “decision point” determines the Anthrobot size and shape.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types

claims.label: Non-movers, linear and circular bots map onto morphotypes 1, 2 and 3
claims.statement: Anthrobot behaviour and morphology are significantly associated: non-moving bots fall mostly in morphotype 1 (small, smooth, spherical), linear movers mostly in morphotype 2 (large, non-polarized cilia) and circular movers mostly in morphotype 3 (polarized cilia), and no displacing bot was found in morphotype 1.
claims.quote: We have further computed the statistical significance of these overlaps (using the Fisher test, see Materials and Methods) and conclude that the non‐movers, linear, and circulars significantly correspond with the morphotypes 1, 2 and 3, respectively.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated

claims.label: Spherical bots with uniform cilia may not move because ciliary forces cancel
claims.statement: Morphotype 1 Anthrobots are likely non-movers or stationary wigglers, which the authors suggest may be because their radially symmetric spherical shape with evenly distributed cilia makes ciliary propulsion forces cancel out, with small imbalances producing only wiggling.
claims.quote: This may be attributable to their spherical shape with homogeneously distributed cilia where the propulsion forces generated by the ciliary motion are more prone to canceling each other out due to the radially symmetric spherical shape, resulting in little or no movement.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated

claims.label: Linear-moving Anthrobots are more bilaterally symmetric about their movement axis
claims.statement: Linear-moving Anthrobots show higher bilateral symmetry of cilia distribution about their axis of movement than circular movers; for circular bots, but not linear bots, the 90-degree rotated axis is more symmetric than the movement axis (p = 0.048), supporting distinct local symmetry profiles for distinct movement types.
claims.quote: Taken together, these findings support our hypothesis that Anthrobots with distinct movement types have distinct local bilateral symmetry profiles, with linear bots showing higher bilateral symmetry.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis

claims.label: Anthrobots recapitulate the bilateral symmetry of many wild-type species
claims.statement: The link between straight-line movement and bilateral symmetry in Anthrobots suggests that these synthetic forms, self-assembling in a symmetrical environment, recapitulate a fundamental morphological property seen in many wild-type species and could be used to study how embryos establish a single body midplane.
claims.quote: This suggests that these synthetic forms recapitulate a fundamental morphological property observed in many wild‐type species.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis

claims.label: Faster and more rotational Anthrobots cover more of a neuronal scratch
claims.statement: Anthrobots can move across scratches in human neuronal monolayers in vitro, and bots with higher rotational tendency or higher speed cover a larger proportion of unique positions along the scratch interface.
claims.quote: Taken together, these data reveal that Anthrobots are capable of efficiently moving across damaged tissues, and that bots that have a higher rotational tendency and or higher speed have higher degrees of unique coordinate coverage by moving across a higher percentage of the scratch interface.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro

claims.label: An intermediate gyration maximizes how closely Anthrobots track scratch edges
claims.statement: In a constrained set of 13 Anthrobots in neuronal scratches, gyration (rotational tendency) has a quadratic relationship with how closely a bot's trajectory follows the scratch edge (p = 0.006), suggesting an intermediate gyration range maximizes edge tracking.
claims.quote: With our constrained dataset, we saw that gyration had a quadratic effect on scratch‐trajectory similarity (Figure 5E) with p = 0.006, suggesting that there is a specific range for gyration where the scratch‐trajectory correlation can be maximized
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro

claims.label: Superbot bridges induce neuronal gap closure in scratched monolayers
claims.statement: Fused Anthrobot assemblies (superbots) placed across a scratch in a human neuronal monolayer induce substantial regrowth of neuronal tissue beneath them within 72 hours, forming a stitch that connects the two sides of the scratch.
claims.quote: Strikingly, within the next 72 h upon inoculation of the superbot into the tissue scratch on day 0, we observed a substantial regrowth of the native tissue taking place (i.e., gap closure), resulting in the formation of a stitch right underneath the “superbot bridge,” connecting the two sides of the scratch (Figure 6B).
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues

claims.label: Superbot-induced gap closure is local and restores native tissue density
claims.statement: Neuronal gap closure occurs only at the site where a superbot is placed; the neuronal coverage density there is statistically indistinguishable from intact tissue outside the scratch, while adjacent and distant parts of the scratch have significantly lower coverage.
claims.quote: Thus, the density of the induced gap closure area that formed as a result of the presence of the superbot represented full (statistically indistinguishable from 100%) recovery of the original tissue and was uniquely different from the surrounding scratch area.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues

claims.label: Passive mechanical loading does not reproduce Anthrobot-induced neural repair
claims.statement: Placing a piece of agarose on neuronal scratches for 4 days to provide passive mechanical loading induces no repair, indicating that simple mechanical contact is not sufficient for the gap closure seen with Anthrobot superbots.
claims.quote: Finally, in order to test whether simple (passive) mechanical contact was sufficient to induce the same effect, we incubated neuronal scratches for 4 days with a piece of agarose on top to provide mechanical loading; this induced no repair (see Figure S11, Supporting Information).
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues

claims.label: Anthrobots and Xenobots share similar movement types and transition profiles
claims.statement: Anthrobots and Xenobots both show discrete movement types with very low interconversion between linear and circular motion (0.2% and 0.3% for Anthrobots, 0.5% and 1.6% for Xenobots) and highly consistent circular behaviour (92% and 95%), though Anthrobot linear behaviour is more consistent (80% versus 67%).
claims.quote: The interconversion between linear and circular is very small for Xenobots (0.5% and 1.6%) and Anthrobots (0.2% and 0.3%), while their consistency of Circular behavior is extremely high for Xenobots (95%) just like for Anthrobots (92%).
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

claims.label: Similar forms from divergent genomes point to generic laws of morphogenesis
claims.statement: Because Anthrobots and Xenobots, despite highly divergent genomes, ages and tissue origins, assemble into very similar kinds of motile constructs, the authors conclude that generic laws of morphogenesis matter in addition to species-specific genomic information.
claims.quote: Despite their highly divergent genome, age, and tissue origin, the two platforms assemble into very similar types of creatures, illustrating the importance of generic laws of morphogenesis[ 31 ] in addition to species‐specific genomic information.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

claims.label: Superbot size is set by bot number and fusion requires exposed basal layers
claims.statement: Anthrobots fuse into larger superbots only in the days immediately after release from the matrix, while their basal layers are still exposed and can mediate bot-to-bot fusion, and superbot size can be controlled by the number of Anthrobots cultured together in a well.
claims.quote: The tendency of the bots to fuse together and thus form different sized collectives (i.e., superbots) for different scratches can be controlled by modulating the number of Anthrobots cultured together in the same well for fusion, which happens only on days immediately following dissolution while the Anthrobot basal layers are still exposed and thus can mediate the bot‐to‐bot fusion.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

claims.label: Tracheal cells healing neural tissue could not be predicted from current models
claims.statement: That wild-type cells from the trachea move over and heal neural tissue is unexpected given their normal role in the body and could not be predicted from any current molecular or tissue-level model, which suggests screening engineered tissue interactions to uncover novel cell capabilities.
claims.quote: The finding is unexpected given these tissues’ normal roles in the human body – the fact that wild‐type cells from trachea will move over and heal neural tissues could not be predicted from any current molecular or tissue‐level models.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

claims.label: Patient-derived Anthrobots could be deployed in vivo without an immune response
claims.statement: Because Anthrobots are made from adult human tissue, they could in future be personalized for each patient and deployed in that patient's body without triggering an immune response.
claims.quote: Anthrobots are derived from adult human tissue, and in the future could be personalized for each patient, enabling safe in‐vivo deployment of these robots in the human body without triggering an immune response.
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

claims.label: Anthrobots may be made from other ciliated human cells such as oviduct or ependyma
claims.statement: Anthrobots may be generable from other ciliated human cells, such as oviductal epithelium or brain ependymal cells, and non-ciliated cell types could be used for bots that need no autonomous motility.
claims.quote: Anthrobots may be able to be generated from other ciliated cells in the human body (e.g., oviductal epithelia or brain ependymal cells), and other cell types can be used for bots when autonomous motility is not needed
claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Conclusion

claims.label: One genome yielding diverse forms in different environments could shape evolution
claims.statement: The additional morphogenetic competencies revealed by Anthrobots could matter for evolutionary developmental biology, since the evolution of anatomical and functional features could be affected by the ability of the same genome to produce very diverse forms in different environments.
